The regression was a double-negated condition in `group_comments()` in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py. The code read:

```python
eidx, end = tlist.token_not_matching(...)
if not (end is not None):
    eidx, end = tlist.token_prev(eidx, skip_ws=False)
    tlist.group_tokens(sql.Comment, tidx, eidx)
```

This inverted the intended logic: it called `group_tokens` precisely when `end` was `None` (i.e., the comment ran to the end of the token list), passing `eidx=None` into `TokenList.group_tokens`, which computes `end_idx = end + include_end` → `None + True`, raising `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'bool'`.

Fixed by correcting the condition to `if end is not None:`, so the trailing-comment grouping step only runs when a valid end token was actually found, matching the original intended behavior (and leaving the "comment runs to end of list" case to be handled correctly elsewhere, as it was before the regression).

Verified with a smoke test covering single-line comments, multi-line comments, SQL hints, and comments at the very end of a statement (both `--` and `/* */` styles, with nothing following) — all produce the expected stripped output with no exception. function.name: run

structured_output.content:
The regression was a double-negated condition in `group_comments()` in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py:

```python
eidx, end = tlist.token_not_matching(...)
if not (end is not None):
    eidx, end = tlist.token_prev(eidx, skip_ws=False)
    tlist.group_tokens(sql.Comment, tidx, eidx)
```

This inverted the intended logic: it called `group_tokens` precisely when `end` was `None` (comment runs to end of token list), passing `eidx=None` into `TokenList.group_tokens`, which computes `end_idx = end + include_end` → `None + True`, raising `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'bool'`.

Fixed by correcting the condition to `if end is not None:`, so the trailing-comment grouping adjustment only runs when a valid non-comment end token was actually found (meaning the comment block does NOT run to the end of the list), which is the correct original logic.

Verified with a smoke test covering single-line comments, multi-line comments, SQL hints, and comments at the very end of a statement (both `--` and `/* */` styles) — all produce correct stripped output with no exception. The temporary smoke test file was removed afterward.

arguments.summary: Fixed regression in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py's group_comments(): corrected an inverted condition `if not (end is not None):` to `if end is not None:`. The bug caused group_tokens to be called with eidx=None whenever a comment ran to the end of a token list, triggering `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'bool'` inside TokenList.group_tokens (end + include_end). This broke strip_comments and related formatting behavior. Verified the fix with manual smoke tests covering single-line, multi-line, SQL-hint, and trailing comments; all now format correctly without error.

message.content:
The regression was a double-negated condition in `group_comments()` in sqlparse/engine/grouping.py:

```python
eidx, end = tlist.token_not_matching(...)
if not (end is not None):
    eidx, end = tlist.token_prev(eidx, skip_ws=False)
    tlist.group_tokens(sql.Comment, tidx, eidx)
```

This inverted the intended logic: it called `group_tokens` precisely when `end` was `None` (comment runs to end of token list), passing `eidx=None` into `TokenList.group_tokens`, which computes `end_idx = end + include_end` → `None + True`, raising `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'bool'`.

Fixed by correcting the condition to `if end is not None:`, so the trailing-comment grouping adjustment only runs when a valid non-comment end token was actually found (meaning the comment block does NOT run to the end of the list), which is the correct original logic.

Verified with a smoke test covering single-line comments, multi-line comments, SQL hints, and comments at the very end of a statement (both `--` and `/* */` styles) — all produce correct stripped output with no exception. The temporary smoke test file was removed afterward.
